title: Bounded evidence-bearing selection of a narrative bridge between two observations
independentExamples: A nonce reactor is initially inactive and later emits a signal; inserting an activation event is supported when a declared transition connects inactive, activation, and emitting states.
A nonce courier starts at one location and is later recorded elsewhere; a travel event is supported only when declared spatial and temporal relations permit that transition.
inputTypes: two or more typed candidate bridge event sequences
provenance-bearing causal temporal goal social and state evidence
preconditions: Every observation and candidate is compiled into explicit events, participants, roles, polarity, time, modality, and state effects.
Candidate support and contradiction use declared KB relations with provenance rather than benchmark-local vocabulary.
The ranking policy defines a positive decision margin and returns unknown for ties or insufficient evidence.
invariants: A candidate is evaluated in the temporal middle, against both the preceding and following observation.
Renaming every entity, predicate, state value, and surface token while preserving typed relations leaves the result unchanged.
Reversing a causal edge, removing an enabling condition, or replacing the bridge with an unrelated event changes support or yields unknown.
No default candidate position, lexical cue, source ID, expected label, or benchmark identity contributes to ranking.
uncertaintySemantics: Defeasible ranking over explicit evidence; ties, incompatible evidence, and missing knowledge remain distinct unknown outcomes and are not resolved by source order.
proofBehavior: A solved result would cite the before event, selected bridge, after event, every activated causal or state transition, every contradiction, feature contributions, provider provenance, and the winning margin.
resourceBounds: At most a declared number of candidates, bridge events, provider records, state expansions, causal expansions, and deterministic search steps; exhaustion returns RESOURCE_LIMIT.
interaction: This would be a new task operation, not an alias for select-narrative-continuation. It may reuse narrative event frames and provider evidence envelopes, but must account for the later observation explicitly.
kbMigration: No migration is authorized. Future provider records would require reviewed causal, temporal, goal, social, and state relation schemas before this method can consume them.
guardianReasons: The current narrative compiler extracts shallow bounded features but does not produce the causal, role, goal, temporal, and state structures required by the proposed preconditions.
The current KB providers do not establish complete or calibrated commonsense evidence for arbitrary ART events.
Reusing the continuation ranker would score a candidate in the wrong temporal position and would not validate compatibility with the later observation.
Without typed evidence, any executable candidate would reduce to lexical or positional policy and fail the semantic rename and contrastive gates.
